prose.title: HammerTime Has No Holes and No Quarterback
prose.dek: Eric Martel paid {{f.team.0005.trade_blind_bid_cash}} to move Jalen Hurts in April, turned the savings into Kenneth Walker and David Montgomery, and has kept a lineup with no holes all summer. His quarterbacks rank last in the league. The preseason simulation ranks the {{f.team.0005.hist_title_years}} champion {{f.team.0005.power_rank|ord}}.

paragraphs: April was deep. Martel carried {{f.team.0005.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0005.cap_opening}} in salary, with {{f.team.0005.studs_opening}} top-twelve starters, Ja'Marr Chase, an Elite WR1, Trey McBride, an Elite TE1, Kenneth Walker and T.J. Hockenson in the superflex, and {{f.team.0005.holes_opening}} holes. C.J. Stroud, Javonte Williams, Ladd McConkey, Montgomery and Luther Burden were all solid. It is also a lineup whose best quarterback grades as a Low-end QB2.

The spring was a salary swap. In March Martel extended Stroud's rookie deal for one more year at {{f.team.0005.contract_16150_salary}}. In April he sent Jalen Hurts and {{f.team.0005.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money to the Long Haulers for their 2027 first and second, which is paying to move a {{f.team.0005.trade1_salary_out}} quarterback, then spent his own 2027 first on Walker and his own second on Montgomery. Before the draft {{f.team.0005.trade_salary_out_s1}} of salary went out and {{f.team.0005.trade_salary_in_s1}} came in. Of his other expiring rookies, Sean Tucker went to Sex Manther at the Expired Rookie Auction and Tyree Wilson was let go.

t.0005.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: Martel tagged Javonte Williams in May at {{f.team.0005.contract_15256_salary}}, and unlike the other tags this summer this one was simply a keep: Williams is his second running back and grades as a High-end RB2. On draft day he moved up twice, sending 4.01, 4.08, 5.01 and two 2027 picks away for 2.12 and 3.08, and made {{f.team.0005.rookie_picks_count}} picks, Skyler Bell and Demond Claiborne first. The only release before the lock cost something small: Troy Franklin, {{f.team.0005.cut_16619_salary}} of salary with a {{f.team.0005.cut_16619_penalty}} penalty.

t.0005.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: With no hole to fill, Martel spent {{f.team.0005.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction mostly on depth and defense. Josh Jacobs was the big buy at {{f.team.0005.faa_14073_price}}, and Aidan Hutchinson, Micah Parsons, Ernest Jones and T.J. Watt came cheaply behind him. Jacobs, a Low-end RB2, is the one Good buy in the What it bought column, and the league table ranks the money {{f.team.0005.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for what each dollar added, which says less about the auction than about how little there was to add.

The contracts were long. Jacobs signed a back-loaded deal at {{f.team.0005.contract_14073_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0005.contract_14073_tcv}} in all, and Hutchinson, Jones and Parsons got multi-year deals too. There were no restructures. After the auction he cut Jonnu Smith, whose {{f.team.0005.cut_13193_salary}} salary carried a {{f.team.0005.cut_13193_penalty}} penalty charged to 2027, and claimed {{f.team.0005.pickups_s3}} players off waivers, among them Quentin Lake and Jalen Nailor.

The lineup it built still has {{f.team.0005.holes_today}} holes and {{f.team.0005.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Chase, McBride, Walker and Hockenson, with the league's best tight ends and its second-best receivers. The hole that the count does not show is under center: Stroud is the only quarterback in it, a tight end plays the superflex, and his quarterbacks rank {{f.team.0005.qb_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}. The defense and the kicker are footnotes, and good ones.

t.0005.faa_value.title: What every owner's auction money bought

t.0005.moves_s3.title: From the auction to week one

captions.t.0005.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close, for every dollar he spent on quarterbacks, backs, receivers and tight ends at the Free Agent Auction. What it bought sorts those buys by grade at their position: Elite, Very good, Good or Depth.

paragraphs: Martel is one of the league's newer owners, here since {{f.team.0005.hist_first_season}}, and he has made the most of it: a title in {{f.team.0005.hist_title_years}}, a division title in {{f.team.0005.hist_div_title_years}}, {{f.team.0005.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips in {{f.team.0005.hist_seasons}} seasons, and a {{f.team.0005.hist_allplay_pct}} career all-play record.

Outlast PG Time holds the last two champions, Pure Greatness and HammerTime, and the simulation has them in that order: Pure Greatness {{f.league.power_rank_0004|ord}}, HammerTime {{f.team.0005.power_rank|ord}}, the Long Haulers {{f.league.power_rank_0006|ord}}. That is a {{f.team.0005.sim_p_division}} chance at defending the division, {{f.team.0005.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and {{f.team.0005.sim_p_title}} title odds, with Cutting and Cross five times each.

The next three years, entered into the record. Finding one, 2027: HammerTime wins the division on the strength of Chase and McBride, and precedent dictates a ruling on the quarterback question, which is deferred. Finding two, 2028: a quarterback is acquired at considerable expense and at least four GIFs. Finding three, 2029: a second title, followed by a closing argument that ends in I rest my case. Ruling: likely, pending appeal.

Week one has started with a waiver pickup leading the way: with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Quentin Lake had an interception and HammerTime has {{f.team.0005.wk_points_final}} points in the bank.
